analysis: Examined the PR's two changes. (1) docs/reference/protocol-messages.md lines 757-765 add a documentation-only paragraph on streamed `auto` tool-call chunking in `inference_response_chunk`. It describes how delta.tool_calls entries share an index and how fragments are concatenated. It changes no wire fields, encryption behavior, or authorization. The existing `data` and `encrypted_data` rules (empty `data` when E2E is active, T-008) are unchanged, so the text introduces no plaintext fallback. The remaining units (lines 584-954, 955-1309, 1310-1460) are unchanged context; I saw nothing in them that conflicts with the threat model. (2) The libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule pointer moves from 889fe3cc to 756432c8. The submodule contents and diff are not supplied, so I cannot evaluate them. The doc cites MLXOpenAIService.swift `streamChatCompletionFrames`, which runs in the native inference engine (TB-007) and is the code that emits tool-call chunks. That code could affect TB-002 (output encryption, T-008), TB-007 (the prefix cache, T-041, and in-process memory handling), the GLM and MiMo prompt-contract handling the doc mentions, or inference cancellation (T-010). I found no evidence of a regression, but this is a coverage limit, not a clearance. The submodule bump should be reviewed separately at the mlx-swift-lm repo diff, in particular for any change to the tool-call streaming path, request-body parsing, cache-scope and salt handling, and any logging of decrypted content. Cross-file: the doc paragraph should be checked against the submodule's streaming implementation, to confirm the chunks are still sealed by the provider's encryption layer (ProviderCore) and that nothing emits plaintext on encryption failure.
